response.title: which power stations start a refrigerator or freezer without tripping
response.answer:
To start a refrigerator or freezer without tripping, the most important specification is the power station's surge (peak) wattage, not just its battery capacity.

Refrigerators and freezers have compressors that briefly draw much more power when starting than when running.

How much power do you need?

Appliance

Mini fridge

Large refrigerator

Chest freezer

	

80–200W

	

500–1,200W




Large upright freezer

	

150–350W

	

1,000–2,000W+

These are approximate ranges; older compressors and some larger appliances can exceed them.

My recommendation: For a typical full-size refrigerator or freezer, look for a power station with at least 1,800–2,000W continuous AC output and sufficient short-duration surge capacity. A 3,000W-class inverter provides more margin, particularly for older appliances.

Another strong 2kWh-class option, particularly if portability matters.

Why even a powerful station can trip

A compressor can demand a large instantaneous current before the inverter responds. Also, some advertised boost modes lower voltage to support high-wattage loads; those modes aren't necessarily suitable for compressor motors. EcoFlow, for example, says its X-Boost feature is more appropriate for heating appliances. 
EcoFlow Manuals

For reliable operation, prioritize genuine motor-starting surge capability, pure sine wave AC output, and a station that keeps its AC outlets enabled between compressor cycles.

markup:
To start a refrigerator or freezer without tripping, the most important specification is the power station's **surge (peak) wattage**, not just its battery capacity.

Refrigerators and freezers have compressors that briefly draw much more power when starting than when running.

## How much power do you need?

| Appliance | Typical running watts | Possible startup surge |
|---|---:|---:|
| Mini fridge | 50–100W | 300–600W |
| Standard refrigerator | 100–250W | 600–1,500W |
| Large refrigerator | 150–400W | 1,000–2,000W+ |
| Chest freezer | 80–200W | 500–1,200W |
| Large upright freezer | 150–350W | 1,000–2,000W+ |

These are approximate ranges; older compressors and some larger appliances can exceed them.

**My recommendation:** For a typical full-size refrigerator or freezer, look for a power station with at least **1,800–2,000W continuous AC output** and sufficient short-duration surge capacity. A 3,000W-class inverter provides more margin, particularly for older appliances.

These are strong candidates based on their inverter specifications, although no model is guaranteed to start every compressor.
